p.s: I think that young people nowadays have a lot more responsibilities and many more things to do besides school than they used to have twenty years ago.
Back then, pupils used to go come home, do their homework and then help their families doing housework, watching their little siblings or helping neighbours cutting the gras.
Nowadays, parents expect more from their children.
They want them to be successful in sports, playing an instrument, or spelling competitions.
So i think, it all depends on what the parens expect their children to do.
There are parents, who do n't make or let their children join activity groups besides school, and others who make their children take part in more activities and competitions than they want.
Thats why many young people do n't have the time to help their communities, even though some of them would like to do that.

There are many young people who are too buisy to help their communities, because they 're put under pressure to be magnificent at school, graduate from college and get their doctors degree as fast as possible, which did n't always use to be like that.

Only rich parents could afford to give their kids a higher education, make them play one or even more instruments and offer them activities besides school, because they had enough money, to hire people, who cleaned their house, cooked their meals and watched their kids.
In spite of that, poorer families could not afford that, so after the basic school education, young people had to work and support their communities as much as possible.
It 's all up to parents and the environment young people grow up in.
